title: Early warning — resting HR and temperature
description: Resting heart rate and body temperature drift before symptoms do. What matters is the deviation from your own recent baseline, not the absolute number, so every panel here is a comparison against a rolling window.

panels.title: Today vs baseline
panels.description: Latest night against its own 30-day mean. Two or three consecutive days of elevated resting HR and temperature is the classic pre-symptomatic pattern.

targets.rawSql:
-- Rolling means are computed over the full history first; filtering earlier would
-- shrink the window at the left edge and quietly change the baseline.
with rolled as (
    select
        day,
        rhr_lowest,
        temp_deviation,
        hrv_avg,
        avg(rhr_lowest)  over w30 as rhr_30,
        avg(hrv_avg)     over w30 as hrv_30
    from daily
    window w30 as (order by day rows between 29 preceding and 1 preceding)
)
select
    round(rhr_lowest - rhr_30, 1) as "Resting HR vs 30d",
    round(temp_deviation, 2)      as "Temp deviation",
    round(hrv_avg - hrv_30, 1)    as "HRV vs 30d"
from rolled
where rhr_lowest is not null
order by day desc
limit 1

panels.title: Resting heart rate — 30 / 90 / 365-day rolling
panels.description: The nightly value is noisy; the crossings matter. A nightly line pulling away from its 30-day mean while the 90-day sits flat is the signal.

targets.rawSql:
with rolled as (
    select
        day::timestamptz as t,
        rhr_lowest,
        avg(rhr_lowest) over (order by day rows between  29 preceding and current row) as r30,
        avg(rhr_lowest) over (order by day rows between  89 preceding and current row) as r90,
        avg(rhr_lowest) over (order by day rows between 364 preceding and current row) as r365
    from daily
    where rhr_lowest is not null
)
select t as "time", 'Nightly'  as metric, rhr_lowest as value from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
union all
select t, '30-day',  r30  from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
union all
select t, '90-day',  r90  from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
union all
select t, '365-day', r365 from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
order by 1

panels.title: Temperature deviation — 30 / 90 / 365-day rolling
panels.description: Oura already reports this as a deviation from your own baseline, so zero is normal and the sign carries the meaning. Sustained positive drift is the illness signal; a single spike usually is not.

targets.rawSql:
with rolled as (
    select
        day::timestamptz as t,
        temp_deviation,
        avg(temp_deviation) over (order by day rows between  29 preceding and current row) as d30,
        avg(temp_deviation) over (order by day rows between  89 preceding and current row) as d90,
        avg(temp_deviation) over (order by day rows between 364 preceding and current row) as d365
    from daily
    where temp_deviation is not null
)
select t as "time", 'Nightly'  as metric, temp_deviation as value from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
union all
select t, '30-day',  d30  from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
union all
select t, '90-day',  d90  from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
union all
select t, '365-day', d365 from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
order by 1

panels.title: Nightly HRV against its own baseline
panels.description: HRV is too noisy night to night to read directly. The 7-day mean against the 30-day is the part worth reacting to.

targets.rawSql:
with rolled as (
    select
        day::timestamptz as t,
        hrv_avg,
        avg(hrv_avg) over (order by day rows between  6 preceding and current row) as h7,
        avg(hrv_avg) over (order by day rows between 29 preceding and current row) as h30
    from daily
    where hrv_avg is not null
)
select t as "time", 'Nightly' as metric, hrv_avg as value from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
union all
select t, '7-day',  h7  from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
union all
select t, '30-day', h30 from rolled where $__timeFilter(t)
order by 1
